stories.headline: Alberta announces fall referendum on separation, triggering national unity response from Carney, Poilievre, and others
stories.summary: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced a two-step October referendum asking voters whether Alberta should pursue a binding separation vote. The announcement triggered a national unity response: PM Carney called Alberta 'essential' and vowed to keep working on energy deals, Conservative Leader Poilievre pledged all Conservative MPs would campaign for a united Canada, and Alberta NDP Leader Nenshi condemned the move. The story dominated coverage from May 21–24.

stories.headline: US suspends Permanent Joint Board on Defence with Canada, Carney downplays significance
stories.summary: The Trump administration suspended the Permanent Joint Board on Defence, a bilateral security body dating to World War II, in a move widely interpreted as a pressure tactic related to Canada's defence spending and F-35 procurement decisions. PM Carney said Canada would continue coordinating with the US while 'diversifying' defence cooperation toward NATO partners and Ukraine. The story generated debate about Canada's NORAD participation.

stories.headline: Carney to visit New York to pitch Canada as investment destination ahead of CUSMA review
stories.summary: PM Carney announced a two-day visit to New York City (May 27–28) to meet with investors, CEOs, and money managers and speak at the Economic Club of New York, framing Canada as a stable destination for capital. The trip was announced as CUSMA trade talks with the US remained stalled and the CRTC streaming dispute added tension.

stories.headline: CRTC streaming content levy triggers US trade tensions and Poilievre attack on Carney
stories.summary: Canada's broadcast regulator ordered major streaming platforms including Netflix and Amazon to contribute 15% of revenues to Canadian content, prompting US accusations that Canada was targeting American companies. Conservative Leader Poilievre demanded Carney overrule the CRTC, warning of US retaliation. The Carney government said it was 'reviewing' the decision.

The Globe and Mail noted the US and Mexico were holding initial USMCA talks in Mexico City without Canada. Politico's Canada Playbook flagged Conservative criticism of Carney's rapprochement with China as a proposed hedge against the US.

stories.summary: Multiple polls released this week show the Carney Liberals at record-high approval ratings, with one Abacus survey describing Liberal support and government approval at new highs as Canadians increasingly see Carney as a stabilizing force against external threats. Projections suggest Liberals would win an increased majority if an election were held now.

stories.headline: Fourteen Liberal MPs warn Carney that Alberta pipeline deal risks environmental credibility
stories.summary: Fourteen Liberal MPs sent a letter to PM Carney at the end of April warning that concessions to Alberta on pipelines and carbon pricing risked the party's environmental credibility. The letter became public this week as Carney signed a new agreement with Premier Smith that includes a path toward an oil pipeline to the Pacific Coast. Former minister Steven Guilbeault was the only MP to publicly criticize the deal.

stories.headline: Carney meets BC Premier Eby on pipeline, warns against delays in major project approvals
stories.summary: PM Carney visited British Columbia to meet with Premier David Eby, pressing for BC's agreement on a new oil pipeline from Alberta to the Pacific Coast and laying out preconditions including First Nations consultation obligations and economic benefits for BC. Carney warned the federal government would invest elsewhere if 'things get stalled' in BC. Eby signalled negotiations were ongoing while expressing concerns about rewarding Alberta separatist behaviour.

Carney is reported to be possibly the first Canadian to hoist the World Cup trophy, an honour typically reserved for tournament winners.

stories.headline: Carney government considering labour law changes including limits on right to strike
stories.summary: Union leaders warned publicly that the Carney government is consulting on changes to the Canada Labour Code that could expand 'essential services' designations and curtail the right to strike in federally regulated workplaces. The government said consultations are needed as Canada faces 'immense stress' and Carney's infrastructure-building agenda requires labour stability.

stories.headline: Poilievre campaigns in BC on property rights following Indigenous land title ruling
stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre made a multi-day visit to BC to campaign on private property rights in light of a Supreme Court ruling on the Cowichan Valley land title case, calling for a Conservative motion instructing federal lawyers to prioritize property rights in court arguments. A First Nation whose rights were at issue stated there was no intent to claim private property. Poilievre also called for action on BC extortion rings.

stories.headline: Canadian inflation hits 2.8% in April; Bank of Canada expected to hold rates in June
stories.summary: Statistics Canada reported Canada's CPI rose to 2.8% in April, a 23-month high, driven largely by energy prices. However, the Bank of Canada's preferred core measures (CPI-trim and CPI-median) decelerated, with most economists concluding the BoC will hold its overnight rate at 2.25% at its June 10 decision. The Bank of Canada also planned to release its Financial Stability Report the week of May 27.

stories.headline: Quebec sovereignty movement OUI Québec releases civil society report calling for 'Quiet Revolution 2.0'
stories.summary: The sovereigntist organization OUI Québec held a weekend gathering in Montreal and released a report based on consultations with 50 civil society organizations, concluding that Quebec's independence movement has replaced pride with insularity and must better include newcomers. The group called for a sovereignty project driven by civil society rather than political parties, ahead of Quebec's October provincial election.

stories.headline: Quebec election polls show three-way race as CAQ surges under new Premier Fréchette
stories.summary: New polling shows the Parti Québécois leading at approximately 30% provincially, followed closely by the PLQ at 28%, with the Coalition Avenir Québec surging to 22% — up 9 points since April — under newly installed Premier Christine Fréchette. Seat projections show the race has tightened significantly ahead of the October 2026 provincial election.

Former Hamilton Centre MP Matthew Green was appointed as interim national director for three months. Lewis pushed back against characterizations that the party is on 'life support.'

stories.headline: BC Conservative Party leadership vote underway amid late controversy over candidate Kerry-Lynne Findlay
stories.summary: Voting opened in the BC Conservative Party leadership race on May 23 with five candidates on the ballot. A late controversy arose over whether to disqualify candidate Kerry-Lynne Findlay over allegations tied to her failed federal re-election campaign, but she was ultimately allowed to remain on the ballot. The winner is to be announced May 30.

stories.headline: RCMP refuses to release full text of China policing agreement despite Conservative and NDP demands
stories.summary: The RCMP declined to release the full memorandum of understanding it signed with China's Ministry of Public Security in January, saying it required Beijing's consent, despite public letters from Conservative and NDP MPs demanding transparency. The agreement 'outlines specific forms of mutual collaboration' but no further details were provided.
